content:
The test image shows a corn ear (pod) with dark green mold growing between and on kernels. The kernels are orange/yellow underneath but heavily covered with a dark green fungal growth across most of the ear surface.

Key features: dark blue-green mold, growing between kernels, covering much of the cob surface.

Top candidates: Trichoderma_Ear_Rot (dark blue-green conidia between kernels), Aspergillus_Ear_Rot (olive-green powdery mold).

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate:

The Trichoderma_Ear_Rot seed reference is a near-perfect match to the test image. Both show:
- Orange/yellow kernels with dark blue-green mold growing between kernels
- Dense mold filling the crevices between kernels
- Coverage across the ear surface

This is clearly distinct from Aspergillus (which is a dusty olive powder at the tip).

```json
{"prediction": "Trichoderma_Ear_Rot", "confidence": 0.93, "reasoning": "The test image shows dark blue-green mold growing between and on yellow/orange corn kernels, covering much of the ear surface. This matches Trichoderma_Ear_Rot exactly — the dark blue-green conidia filling spaces between kernels is the hallmark feature, confirmed by strong visual match with reference images. Aspergillus shows dusty olive-green powder mainly at the ear tip, which is different from what is seen here."}
```
